methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Amazon bows to local backlash over AI data centers, scraps plans to build four new facilities in Northern Virginia — site to be repurposed for mixed-use and residential development. - Tom's Hardware
signals.signal_reading: Amazon's cancellation of four NoVA data centers signals that even the region's concentrated AI infrastructure advantage faces local resistance and limits, potentially constraining the depth of the existing hub rather than enabling distribution to other regions.

signals.title: AI Ready Roanoke evaluates use for new technology in Roanoke Valley - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: AI Ready Roanoke represents intentional capacity-building outside traditional tech hubs—if successful, this structured evaluation and adoption approach could create distributed deep capability rather than passive platform consumption.

signals.title: Virginia Tech outlines philosophy for AI adoption - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's articulated AI adoption philosophy creates institutional infrastructure for developing deep capability across its distributed campus system and research partnerships, potentially seeding peer learning networks beyond NoVA.

signals.title: JLARC: Data center tax break accounts for 60% of Virginia’s incentive spending
signals.signal_reading: Data center tax breaks consuming 60% of Virginia's incentive spending reveals a policy choice to subsidize concentrated infrastructure over distributed capability development—capital investment without workforce depth or geographic equity.

signals.title: Virginia governor orders statewide plan to address AI cyberattacks - StateScoop
signals.signal_reading: A statewide AI cybersecurity response plan signals platform-level adoption across government—potentially broad but shallow implementation where agencies consume AI-powered security tools without developing deep internal AI expertise.
